harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured a persistent, filesystem-enforced 100 MiB XFS project quota for datauser under /srv/data. Allowed and over-limit writes were tested before and after reboot. RHEL 10.0, kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0, SELinux enforcement, SSH access, and existing software were preserved.
actions_performed: Created the locked datauser account with /srv/data as its home and mode 0700 permissions.
Created a dedicated XFS filesystem backed by /var/lib/datauser-storage.xfs and mounted it persistently with prjquota,nodev,nosuid,noexec.
Assigned /srv/data project ID 1000 and a 102400 KiB hard quota.
Verified a 99 MiB write succeeds and a subsequent write stops precisely at 100 MiB.
Restarted node1 safely and verified its changed boot identity, automatic mount recovery, quota enforcement, data integrity, SSH, SELinux, and unchanged OS/kernel.
Removed all test data; /srv/data is clean and currently uses zero quota blocks.

evidence.summary: Initial and final evidence confirms RHEL 10.0 and kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0 remained unchanged, xfsprogs was already installed, no quota package was added, SELinux remains Enforcing, and SSH remains active and enabled with its configuration checksum unchanged.

/srv/data is an active XFS mount with prjquota; project accounting and enforcement are ON, project ID 1000 is inherited recursively, and its hard limit is 102400 KiB. Persistent configuration validates with zero errors.

evidence.requirement: Allowed and denied behavior as datauser
evidence.summary: As datauser, 99 MiB writes succeeded. Additional writes failed at exactly 102400 KiB project usage. The final post-restart test repeated this behavior and removed all test artifacts afterward.

Healthy baseline boot ID 180a78a0-8a84-45ff-82f1-cd734208a369 was captured; the safe restart was acknowledged; node1 became temporarily unavailable and returned with boot ID c79016c5-503b-4ea3-9d49-acefa0e59bbf. SSH, the XFS mount, filesystem UUID, quota enforcement, account permissions, configuration checksums, and the pre-restart data checksum all recovered correctly.
